purpose: Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including pneumonia, sinus infections, skin infections, and eye infections. It works only against bacteria, so it will not help with colds, flu, or other viral illnesses. Your doctor prescribed it because it targets the specific type of bacteria causing your infection.
how_it_works: Moxifloxacin works by blocking two important proteins that bacteria need to copy and repair their DNA. Without being able to do this, the bacteria cannot survive or multiply. Think of it like removing the instruction manual the bacteria need to keep growing — they eventually die off, and your infection clears up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, and headache. Some people notice stomach upset or vomiting. If you are using the eye drop form, you may feel mild burning, stinging, or temporary blurred vision right after putting the drops in.
warnings: Moxifloxacin carries an important warning about tendon problems — it can cause tendon pain, swelling, or even rupture, especially in older adults or those on steroids. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you feel sudden pain or swelling in a joint or tendon. It can also affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have a heart condition. Avoid prolonged sun exposure, as it can increase your risk of sunburn. This medication may cause nerve damage or muscle weakness in rare cases, so report any tingling, numbness, or weakness right away.
typical_dosing: For most infections, the usual adult dose is one 400 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. It can be taken with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day, and finish the entire course even if you start feeling better early. For eye infections, the typical dose is one drop in the affected eye two to three times daily, depending on which eye drop product you are using.
